summary: Give every organization a curated catalogue of request topics and make the topic the only classifier a caller supplies. One new table (RequestTopic) with a functional case-insensitive unique index per organization and audience, two new nullable columns on Request (topicId, topicLabel), a new topics module in apps/api/src/requests/ behind SessionGuard + OrgScopeGuard with create / rename / archive / restore / whole-audience reorder, seeded at signup inside the existing signup transaction and re-seeded by any read of an audience that holds no row. POST /requests gains a required topicId, derives Request.type from the topic, snapshots the topic name into topicLabel, and refuses type and accessKind in the body; GET /requests gains a topicId filter and a closed status value spanning declined and cancelled. On the web, a new Settings > Request topics screen with up/down reorder controls, a topic picker replacing the type + access-kind controls in the new-request modal, and one exported status label map (Pending / In progress / Completed / Closed, plus a closure sub-label) replacing STATUS_OPTIONS and REQUEST_STATUS_META. Four points of the spec cannot be settled by an implementer and are raised as findings rather than guessed at.

tasks.title: Prisma: the RequestTopic model, the functional unique index, the two nullable Request columns, and the backfill insert

migration.note: One migration for the run. infra/deploy.sh runs the migration as a one-off task on the NEW image at line 183-184 (infra/migrate.sh) and only then tf applies the services at line 187-188, so the schema changes while the PREVIOUS code is still serving. Additive is what makes that window safe: CREATE TABLE "RequestTopic", ALTER TABLE "Request" ADD COLUMN "topicId" TEXT NULL and "topicLabel" VARCHAR(60) NULL, plus the seed INSERT for existing organizations. No rename, no drop, no new NOT NULL on an existing table — the previous code sees one unreferenced table and two nullable columns. The migration step is skipped entirely on a web-only deploy (deploy.sh:168), which is a further reason nothing may depend on it having run.
migration.sql: Uniqueness is a hand-written functional index — CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "RequestTopic_organizationId_audience_name_lower_key" ON "RequestTopic" ("organizationId", "audience", LOWER("name")) — because Prisma @@unique is case-sensitive. This is the device already used at apps/api/prisma/migrations/20260901120000_spec_org_01_clients/migration.sql:30 for Client, and before it by Project, BoardColumn and TaskLabel.

(FK Account, SetNull), archivedAt DateTime?, archivedByAccountId String? (FK Account, SetNull). tasks.title: apps/api: the request-topics controller and service — read, create, rename, archive, restore, reorder, and seed-on-read

migration.note: no schema change in this task

tasks.description: New controller at @Controller('api/organizations/:orgId') with @UseGuards(SessionGuard, OrgScopeGuard), registered in app.module.ts alongside RequestsController (app.module.ts:108) and its service alongside RequestsService (app.module.ts:147). Guard order and the 404-not-403 rule come from apps/api/src/auth/org-scope.guard.ts:22 — queries scope by session.organizationId, which is a required argument with no default on every service method, and the path :orgId is never a selector. The capability refusal must carry REQUEST_TOPIC_MESSAGES.manageForbidden, which CapabilityGuard cannot express: apps/api/src/auth/capability.guard.ts:64 throws a fixed TEMPLATE_MESSAGES.generic.forbidden. Follow the precedent already stated in apps/api/src/holidays/holidays.controller.ts:22-26 and apps/api/src/requests/requests.controller.ts:27-31 and check the capability in the service with can(normalizeRole(role), 'manage-request-topics'), not with @RequireCapability. Routes: GET request-topics (audience optional, status active|archived|all defaulting to active), POST request-topics (201, sortOrder defaults to the audience's highest plus ten), PATCH request-topics/order, PATCH request-topics/:topicId, PATCH request-topics/:topicId/archive, PATCH request-topics/:topicId/restore. The literal 'order' path MUST be declared before the ':topicId' path or Nest matches it as a topic id. There is no DELETE handler and no service method that removes a row. Archive and restore each open a transaction, re-read the row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and evaluate the status guard against that read — never against a copy loaded earlier — so two concurrent archives produce one write and one 409. Reorder rewrites every named topic's sortOrder to its index times ten in one transaction; lock the rows in a canonical order (ORDER BY id), never in the caller-supplied order, or two concurrent reorders deadlock. Seed-on-read (REQ-02-016) writes an audience's defaults when it holds no row of any status — see the risk registered against it.

concurrency.lock: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the topic row inside the archive and restore transactions; the whole audience's rows, locked in id order, inside the reorder transaction

tasks.description: createRequest (requests.service.ts:305) resolves topicId inside the caller's organization: absent/null/'' is 400 topicRequired; archived, another organization's, or naming no row is 400 topicUnavailable with one identical body, which is the deliberate exception to the 404 convention and leaks nothing; an audience that does not match the addressee kind is 400 topicAudienceMismatch, and 'member' is the only addressee kind this spec ships. type is written from the topic and topicLabel is written from the topic's name in the same transaction as the Request row. The serializer gains the topic member on every row and on the detail: name is the snapshot topicLabel, never the catalogue's current name; status is read from the catalogue row so a screen can mark an archived topic. topic is null on a request that carries no topicLabel. risks.risk: The literal path PATCH /request-topics/order collides with PATCH /request-topics/:topicId. Nest matches in declaration order, so a controller that declares :topicId first answers the reorder call as a rename of a topic whose id is the string 'order' — a 404, silently, with every reorder case failing in a way that looks like a routing bug rather than an ordering one.
risks.mitigation: declare the literal route first and assert it in TC-02-INT-22.

risks.risk: The reorder transaction locks every row of one audience. Locking them in the caller-supplied topicIds order lets two concurrent reorders of the same audience, sent in different orders, deadlock — which edge case 12a's 'the later one wins whole' assumes away.
risks.mitigation: lock in a canonical order (ORDER BY id) inside the transaction, never in the order the body listed.

risks.risk: Seed-on-read makes GET a writer. Two concurrent first reads of a catalogue-less organization — which one page load produces, since the picker reads status=active and the topic filter reads status=all — both find nothing and both insert, and the functional unique index fails the loser. The spec prescribes no rule here while prescribing one for every other writer.
risks.mitigation: raised as finding P3; nothing is implemented until the spec says whether the loser retries, re-reads, or answers 500.

risks.risk: Request.accessKind is documented in the schema as 'Required when type = access'. After this spec every new access-type row carries none, so the comment describes a rule the code no longer keeps.
risks.mitigation: amend the comment in T2; the column, its nullability and every stored value are untouched, which is what keeps the migration additive.

risks.risk: REQUEST_MESSAGES.typeUnknown ('Choose a request type') and the removed request-new-type control leave a message emitted by nothing. Deleting it would be a rename of a shared export in the same run as a behaviour change.
risks.mitigation: leave the key in place; it costs nothing and removing it is a separate, deliberate edit.

risks.risk: GET /request-topics defines audience as a closed set that 400s on a typo but says nothing about an unknown status value, while the sibling GET /requests 400s every unknown query value (requests.service.ts:163-172).
risks.mitigation: raised as finding P6; the reasoning printed under TC-02-INT-04 argues for a 400 but no rule says so.

risks.risk: Nine seeded staff topics land on every existing organization through the migration's insert, including organizations that have been curating nothing. This is by design and is what AC-2 asserts, but it is a visible product change to every tenant on the deploy that carries it.
risks.mitigation: the insert is idempotent under the functional unique index, and REQ-02-016 makes the same rows appear on read regardless, so a rollback of the application needs no rollback of the data.
